messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Double-clicking with the mouse on theobject (when the patcher window is locked) opens an editing window in which the contents of text can be viewed and edited. Theobject ignores messages to change its text while the editing window is open. Unlike theobject, changes made in the editing window ofactually alter the contents of the object.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: The message is stored in theobject, placed after any previously stored messages, and is followed by a space.

messages.name: cr
messages.description: Puts a carriage return at the end of the contents of, to start a new line. If the last character inis a space, the carriage return replaces that space.

messages.name: dump
messages.description: The wordcausesto send its contents out of the object's left outlet.

messages.name: filetype
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol, sets the file types which can be read and written into theobject. File types are specified using the standard(e.g. filetype ffoo). The messagewith no arguments restores the default file behavior -- either Max binary or text file formats. File types are mapped to filename extensions on Windows based on the messages to max contained in the file max-fileformats.txt in the init folder, which is loaded on startup. If you are defining your own filetype, you may want to include your own text file in the init folder in order to specify a mapping between an extension and your four-letter type code.

messages.name: line
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, causesto send out the contents of that line number (up to 256 characters) with the wordprepended (for setting the contents of abox). Lines are numbered beginning with 1; any line number message less than 1 is converted to. If a nonexistent line number is requested, nothing is sent out.

messages.name: open
messages.description: Opens the object's text window for editing. Double-clicking on theobject in a locked patcher has the same effect. Theobject ignores messages to change its text while the editing window is open. Unlike theobject, changes made in the editing window ofactually alter the contents of the object. However, these changes will not be saved or communicated to theobject until the editing window is closed.

messages.name: query
messages.description: The wordsends a number that specifies the number of lines stored in theobject out the object's right outlet.

messages.name: read
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies a filename, will read the contents of a text file. If no filename or pathname is specified, themessage will call up the standard Open Document dialog box, so that a text file can be specified. Use the filetype message to use a custom filetype with this object.

messages.name: settitle
messages.description: The word, followed by any word, sets the title of the text window. If you want more than one word to appear as the default text, you must enclose the words in double quotes or precede the spaces with a backslash ().

messages.name: symbol
messages.description: The word, followed by any word, stores that word at the end of the contents of. This is useful if you want to store a word that would otherwise be understood as a specific message by. For example,stores the word, followed by a space, at the end of the contents of, rather than erasing the contents.

messages.name: tab
messages.digest: Place a tab character in the text
messages.description: Puts a tab stop at the end of the contents of. If the last character inis a space, the tab stop replaces that space.

messages.name: wclose
messages.description: Closes the window associated with theobject.

messages.name: write
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies a filename, will save the contents ofas a text file in the current default folder unless the file is specified with an absolute pathname. If no filename or pathname is specified, themessage will open up a standard Save As dialog box, so that the contents ofcan be saved in a separate text file. Use the filetype message to use a custom filetype with this object.Please note that changes to theobject will not be saved until the editing window is closed.
